title: Jesus, Thy Blessings Are Not Few
description: Jesus, Thy Blessings Are Not Few in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 34, headed “[Supplement.] None excluded from hope, Rom. 1. 16. 1 Cor. 1. 24”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Je-sus, thy bless-ings are not few, Nor is thy gos-pel weak; Thy grace can melt the stub-born Jew, And bow th'a-spir-ing Greek.

lines: Jesus, thy blessings are not few,
Nor is thy gospel weak;
Thy grace can melt the stubborn Jew,
And bow th' aspiring Greek.
Wide as the reach of Satan's rage
Doth thy salvation flow;
'Tis not confin'd to sex or age,
The lofty or the low.
While grace is offer'd to the prince,
The poor may take their share;
No mortal has a just pretence
To perish in despair.
Be wise, ye men of strength and wit,
Nor boast your native powers;
But to his sovereign grace submit,
And glory shall be yours.
Come, all ye vilest sinners come,
He'll form your souls anew:
His gospel and his heart have room
For rebels such as you.
His doctrine is almighty love;
There's virtue in his Name
To turn the raven to a dove,
The lion to a lamb.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
